nodes.theorem_title: Theorem 4.6: the Angel of power two wins
nodes.natural_language_statement: There exists a single power-two Angel strategy that makes legal uneaten landings forever against every Devil strategy on the infinite integer lattice, with the Devil moving first and permitted to pass.
nodes.source: Andras Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins, CPC 16 (2007), 363-374; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript internal pagination. Theorem 4.6, manuscript p. 8.

nodes.theorem_title: Theorem 2.7: reduction to a Nice Devil
nodes.formal_statement: theorem AngelDevil.nice_devil_reduction (p : Nat) (hp : 0 < p) : ¬ AngelDevil.AngelWins p → ∃ N, 0 < N ∧ AngelDevil.NiceCanConfine p N := by sorry
nodes.natural_language_statement: For every positive integer power, if the Angel has no winning strategy, some Nice Devil can keep every finite safe play in a fixed box of positive integer radius. This formulation includes the determinacy observation from the introduction in addition to Theorem 2.7.
nodes.source: Andras Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins, CPC 16 (2007), 363-374; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript internal pagination. Theorem 2.7, manuscript p. 3, with the introductory determinacy observation on p. 1.

nodes.theorem_title: Theorem 4.5: power two escapes every Nice Devil
nodes.natural_language_statement: There exists one power-two Angel strategy that survives against every Nice Devil and, against each such opponent, reaches outside every finite box centred at the origin.
nodes.source: Andras Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins, CPC 16 (2007), 363-374; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript internal pagination. Theorem 4.5, manuscript p. 8.

nodes.theorem_title: Angel and Devil: infinite-board game and strategies
nodes.natural_language_statement: Integer lattice game with Devil-first rounds, passing, history-dependent strategies, legal survival, Nice Devil restrictions, unbounded escape, and confinement of every finite safe prefix. Conventions follow Sections 1-2, Definitions 2.2, 2.3, 2.5 and equation (2).
nodes.definition:
import Std

/-! The convention is Mathe's paper: Devil moves first, may pass, and may
eat any square (including the occupied square); only subsequent landing on
an eaten square loses. Zero-length Angel moves are allowed by Definition 2.5.
Histories are stored oldest first. Strategies are total also off legal play.
-/
namespace AngelDevil

abbrev Point := Int × Int
def origin : Point := (0, 0)

def Jump (p : Nat) (u v : Point) : Prop :=
  -(p : Int) ≤ v.1 - u.1 ∧ v.1 - u.1 ≤ (p : Int) ∧
  -(p : Int) ≤ v.2 - u.2 ∧ v.2 - u.2 ≤ (p : Int)

def InBox (N : Nat) (v : Point) : Prop := Jump N origin v

def Journey (p : Nat) (h : List Point) : Prop :=
  h.head? = some origin ∧
  ∀ (i : Nat) (u v : Point), h[i]? = some u → h[i+1]? = some v → Jump p u v

abbrev DevilStrategy := List Point → Option Point
abbrev AngelStrategy := List Point → List (Option Point) → Point

structure State where
  visited : List Point
  burned : List (Option Point)

def initial : State := ⟨[origin], []⟩
def current (s : State) : Point := s.visited.getLastD origin
def step (A : AngelStrategy) (D : DevilStrategy) (s : State) : State :=
  let burned := s.burned ++ [D s.visited]
  ⟨s.visited ++ [A s.visited burned], burned⟩

def play (A : AngelStrategy) (D : DevilStrategy) : Nat → State
  | 0 => initial
  | n+1 => step A D (play A D n)

def Survives (p : Nat) (A : AngelStrategy) (D : DevilStrategy) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, Jump p (current (play A D n)) (current (play A D (n+1))) ∧
    some (current (play A D (n+1))) ∉ (play A D (n+1)).burned

def AngelWins (p : Nat) : Prop := ∃ A, ∀ D, Survives p A D

/- Definition 2.2, as made explicit by equation (2): the origin and every
square reachable from a position before the last one are protected. -/
def Nice (p : Nat) (D : DevilStrategy) : Prop :=
  ∀ h, Journey p h → ∀ z, D h = some z →
    z ≠ origin ∧ ∀ v ∈ h.dropLast, ¬ Jump p v z

def Escapes (A : AngelStrategy) (D : DevilStrategy) : Prop :=
  ∀ N : Nat, ∃ n : Nat, ¬ InBox N (current (play A D n))

def NiceAngelWins (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ A, ∀ D, Nice p D → Survives p A D ∧ Escapes A D

def NiceCanConfine (p N : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ D, Nice p D ∧ ∀ A n,
    (∀ m, m < n →
      Jump p (current (play A D m)) (current (play A D (m+1))) ∧
      some (current (play A D (m+1))) ∉ (play A D (m+1)).burned) →
    InBox N (current (play A D n))

end AngelDevil
nodes.source: Andras Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins, CPC 16 (2007), 363-374; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript internal pagination. Sections 1-2, manuscript pp. 1-3.

nodes.explanation:
Assuming the two paper milestones, the Angel of power two has a winning strategy.
The child statements are open obligations, not conclusions established by this
submission.

Suppose there were no winning power-two Angel strategy. Theorem 2.7, in the
formulation that includes the introduction's determinacy observation, supplies a
positive radius and a Nice Devil that confines every finite safe play to that box.
Theorem 4.5 supplies a single Angel strategy that survives and escapes every box
against every Nice Devil. Apply this strategy to the confining Nice Devil.

Its infinite survival makes each finite prefix safe. Its escape property supplies
a round outside the confining box, while the confinement property places that same
round inside the box. This contradiction proves the main conclusion conditional
on the two imported milestones. This is the last deduction on manuscript page 8,
after Theorem 4.5.
